Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Board’s Unanimous Vote

Ahmed Ishtiaque24 Nov 2026
Assets: NVDA
Jensen Huang, NVDA, Nvidia, Nvidia CEO, Nvidia Shares
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 6:44
Instaread

Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its president and chief executive officer following a unanimous board vote, reversing his sudden departure less than two weeks ago.

The decision returns the company’s co-founder to its top leadership position amid ongoing investigations and heightened scrutiny over national security concerns.

In a November 23 announcement, Nvidia confirmed that Huang had also resumed his position as a member of the board, effective immediately. The decision followed several discussions and meetings between Huang and directors, who said they were satisfied with his candor and ability to lead the company.

The board also considered input from senior U.S. government officials before approving his return. According to Nvidia, that input gave directors confidence that reinstating Huang would not create a national security risk.

Nvidia Board Unanimously Approves Jensen Huang’s Return

Harvey C. Jones, Nvidia’s board chair, said directors believe Huang remains the right person to lead the company through its next phase of growth.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” Jones said in the announcement.

NVIDIA’s board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board director effective immediately, reversing a recent CEO transition. Source: @nvidianewsroom/X

The decision marks a significant reversal from the leadership changes announced earlier in November. On November 12, Nvidia disclosed that Huang had resigned as president, CEO, and board director, effective immediately. The board subsequently appointed longtime finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO while beginning the process of identifying a permanent successor.

Huang’s departure followed reports involving personal relationships and concerns about a possible foreign intelligence operation. Media coverage also raised questions about potential national security implications involving individuals connected to China.

According to subsequent reporting by Reuters and The Associated Press, the circumstances surrounding his departure attracted attention from U.S. authorities and prompted broader scrutiny of the company’s leadership and compliance arrangements.

Huang’s reinstatement does not bring the internal investigation to an end. Nvidia confirmed that the independent committee established to examine reports of a foreign intelligence effort targeting its founder will continue its work until completion.

Foreign Intelligence Investigation Remains Open

Nvidia initially announced its independent investigation on November 8, following reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.

The company appointed a committee consisting exclusively of independent directors and retained outside legal counsel to oversee the inquiry. The board said at the time that it had no reason to believe national security or Nvidia’s confidential information had been compromised, although it intended to examine all available information.

ADVERTISEMENT

The November 23 announcement maintains that commitment. Nvidia said Huang supports the investigation and has agreed to cooperate fully until the process concludes.

The distinction is important: the board’s assessment that his return presents no national security risk does not mean the underlying investigation has been completed.

The company’s latest decision also follows public support for Huang’s return from prominent figures, including U.S. President Donald Trump. Brave New Coin reported that Trump had encouraged Nvidia to bring its founder back after the board initially indicated that reinstatement was not under consideration.

The president subsequently welcomed the reversal, describing it as the correct decision.

Nevertheless, questions surrounding the circumstances of Huang’s departure remain relevant to the company’s governance and regulatory responsibilities. Nvidia has also faced scrutiny over potential export-control and other compliance issues, according to media reports.

Nvidia Establishes New Compliance Oversight

Alongside Huang’s reinstatement, Nvidia is introducing additional governance measures intended to strengthen oversight of national security risks and international trade compliance.

The board has established a National Security and Export Control Committee, consisting entirely of independent directors. Its responsibilities include supervising trade compliance and assessing national security risks associated with the company’s operations.

NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has formed a dedicated committee to oversee national security and export control matters. Source: @nvidianewsroom/X

The committee is also engaging legal counsel with experience in national security matters. Those advisers will bring in additional specialists to support its work.

Nvidia is separately beginning a search for a Chief Compliance Officer. The new executive will oversee compliance across the company and report to the board’s Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee.

These measures indicate that Nvidia intends to maintain closer oversight of regulatory and security-related matters even as Huang returns to executive leadership.

Jones also acknowledged Kress’s contribution during the transition, thanking her for managing the company as interim CEO while continuing her responsibilities as chief financial officer.

Kress will now return to her previous executive responsibilities. She has served as the company’s CFO since September 2013 and has been responsible for overseeing its financial organization during a period of substantial expansion.

Jensen Huang Signals Renewed Commitment to Nvidia

In his statement following the reinstatement, Huang expressed appreciation for the board’s decision and acknowledged the responsibility of returning to lead the company.

“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said.

He also thanked Jones, Kress, Nvidia’s executive team, employees, shareholders, and business partners for their support during the leadership transition.

Jensen Huang updates his X bio and adds “CEO of Nvidia” to his title. Source: @JensenHuang/X

Huang described Nvidia as one of the world’s most consequential technology companies and said he was eager to resume his responsibilities.

His return restores the company’s familiar leadership structure at a time when demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure continues to shape the semiconductor industry.

Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has overseen its transformation from a graphics processing unit manufacturer into a central supplier of computing hardware and software for artificial intelligence, data centers, and accelerated computing.

That history has made his leadership closely associated with the company’s corporate strategy and long-term direction. His unexpected departure therefore created uncertainty around the company’s succession planning and executive decision-making.

Nvidia Stock Rallies Following Leadership Reversal

Financial markets reacted positively to the reinstatement announcement. According to Reuters, Nvidia shares surged approximately 33% in early trading on November 23, as investors responded to the return of its long-serving founder.

The announcement also helped revive sentiment across technology and artificial intelligence stocks following recent weakness in the sector. Reuters reported gains in broader U.S. equity benchmarks, including the Nasdaq and S&P 500, during the session.

However, the immediate market reaction does not resolve the governance and regulatory questions surrounding Nvidia. Investors will continue monitoring the independent investigation, the company’s compliance initiatives, and any further developments involving U.S. authorities.

For now, Huang’s return restores continuity at the top of Nvidia while placing additional responsibility on its board to demonstrate that the company can maintain effective oversight.

The independent investigation will continue, and Nvidia has pledged to cooperate with government inquiries. The outcome of those processes, alongside the implementation of its new compliance framework, will remain important developments for the company in the coming weeks.
